subject.title: [Feature]: Skip dispatch when message mentions a different account's bot

question: Should Matrix add a new opt-in ignoreOtherMentions-style gate for messages that mention a different configured Matrix account, and what should the config contract be?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but this adds channel config and message-suppression semantics where OpenClaw policy requires maintainer intent before automation chooses a default shape.

options.title: Add a narrow Matrix opt-in gate
options.body: Introduce a default-off Matrix plugin config key that drops human room messages mentioning a different configured account before typing or LLM dispatch, with focused handler, schema, and docs coverage.

options.title: Defer until sibling mention metadata is settled
options.body: Keep this issue open behind https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/80432 so inbound suppression uses a clearer roster/mention target contract.

options.title: Reject extra Matrix suppression config
options.body: Keep current requireMention and system-prompt workflows only, accepting token/typing overhead in ambient multi-account rooms.

recommendation.title: Add a narrow Matrix opt-in gate
recommendation.body: Introduce a default-off Matrix plugin config key that drops human room messages mentioning a different configured account before typing or LLM dispatch, with focused handler, schema, and docs coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the Matrix allowBots policy and merged adjacent Matrix mention work, making them the strongest routing candidate for the config/behavior decision.
